newsitem.title: UK: UK's CWS members back moves to fend off takeovers.
newsitem.headline: UK's CWS members back moves to fend off takeovers.

text.p: Members of Britain's mutually-owned Co-Operative Wholesale Society (CWS) on Saturday backed measures to protect the company from further take-over attempts after its recent battle to fend off a hostile bid.

Delegates at the annual meeting voted unanimously in favour of a resolution urging the CWS board to "take all necessary steps to ensure the Society's assets are secured for current and future members."
The resolution followed an unsuccessful 1.2 billion pound ($2 billion) takeover bid last month by British entrepreneur Andrew Regan.
The bid for CWS -- whose interests range from supermarkets to funeral parlours and insurance services -- collapsed after a high court judge described Regan's ethics as "clearly dishonest".
The CWS traces its origins to 1844 and now supplies most of Britain's co-operative retail societies with everything from babyfood to coffins.
The supermarket arm of the group has lagged behind high street competitors, although its bank and chain of opticians and travel agents are profitable.
CWS chairman Lennox Fyfe told the meeting the board would make it a priority to improve business performance across the society.
"Clearly we have to work harder to make our Co-operative aims and aspirations better understood and we have to invest further in the development and expansion of the Co-operative sector," Fyfe said.
"The message today from this meeting to would-be predators is that the assets of this Society are not for sale at any price," he added.
